world.api:
OV.World = {
  step(G, ticks) -> {ticks, stopped, reason:null|'event'|'dogfight'|'battle'|'ended'}   handler order exactly as CAMPAIGN_API §3.1; OV.BaseSim/Economy/Soldiers/Missions are feature-detected; with nothing airborne and no UFO flying it jumps to the next 10-min boundary or the next landed-UFO lift-off (TUNE.GEO_IDLE_COALESCE); result is hash-identical to stepping 5 s at a time
  order(G, craftId, target) -> {ok, reason?, warn?}     target = {kind:'ufo'|'site'|'alienBase'|'base', id} | {kind:'point', lon, lat} | 'home'; reasons noCraft|notReady|inDogfight|noTarget|noSoldiers|noFuel; warns noWeapons|tooSlow|tooFar
  launch(G, craftId, target) -> same, requires status 'ready'      a launch sets out/missionT/patrol=false/lowFuel=false and tops up equipment from base stores
  recall(G, craftId) -> {ok,...}      patrol(G, craftId, lon, lat) -> {ok,...}      canOrder(G, craftId, target) -> {ok, reason?, warn?} (pure)
  loseCraft(G, craftId, reason) -> craftLost event|null      radarCircles(G) -> [{lon, lat, rangeNm, kind:'small_radar'|'large_radar'|'hyper_wave_decoder'|'craft', baseId|craftId}]
  dropTarget(G, kind, id, lon?, lat?)      every airborne non-returning craft whose dest is (kind,id) switches to patrol at that point and gets targetLost
  checkup(G, craftId) -> 'repair'|'rearm'|'refuel'|'ready'      detectChance(G, ufoId, baseId) -> int % (formula of §3.4)
  moveCrafts(G), moveUfos(G), contacts(G), burnFuel(G), patrolDiscovery(G), detect(G), autosave(G)   (single handlers, exported for tests)
}
OV.Missions = {
  planMonth(G) -> [alienMission]      Data.scriptsForMonth; guarded by plannedMonth; sets G.plannedMonth = G.month
  think30m(G); scan10m(G); daily(G); monthEnd(G)      contract steps 10, 6, 15, 17
  spawnMission(G, type, {region?, race?, cityId?, delayMin?, targetBaseId?, alienBaseId?, script?}) -> alienMission
  spawnUfo(G, missionId) -> ufo|null      onUfoWaypoint(G, ufoId)      onUfoLiftOff(G, ufoId)
  onUfoDown(G, ufoId, 'crashed'|'destroyed', craftId|null) -> ufo|null      onSiteCleared(G, siteRef, 'win'|'abort'|'loss')      onResearch(G, topicId)
  removeUfo(G, ufoId) -> ufo|null      removes a UFO, updates its mission's liveUfos and mission end, gives followers targetLost
  regionWeights(G) -> {regionId: weight}      table-mission weights (×3 near a base)
}
G.alien keys added (Missions-owned, plain JSON): pendingPacts [{countryId, missionId}]; newPacts {month, countries:[id]}|null (pacts signed at the last month end); lastReveal {month, alienBaseId}|null (base revealed by agents at the last month end).
New OV.TUNE keys: GEO_MAX_STEPS_PER_FRAME 3, GEO_CHUNK_TICKS 720, GEO_FRAME_BUDGET_MS 12, AUTOSAVE_DAYS [1,10,20], LOW_FUEL_MARGIN_10M 1, BASE_DEFENCE_BASE 1800, BASE_DEFENCE_PER_COEF 300, GEO_IDLE_COALESCE true, UFO_BASE_SIGHT_NM 268, ALIEN_BASE_SUPPLY_PCT 6, RETALIATION_FIRST_MIN 3000, RETALIATION_UFO_REGION_PCT 50, RETALIATION_UFO_REGION_PER_COEF 6, TERROR_CITIES_MEMORY 12.
world.summary:
The Geoscape world simulation is done. OV.World (world.js) runs the clock, craft and UFO flight, radar and fuel. OV.Missions (missions.js) runs the alien strategy. Both follow CAMPAIGN_API.md. 39 new tests pass (geo_world 20, geo_missions 19), about 2.1 s for both files. The full `--strict` suite is 511 passed and 1 failed. The failure is in data_crossref: the Ufopaedia engineer's in-progress pt-PT.ufopaedia.js contains a flagged Brazilian form («Arquivo»). My files are not involved.

**World**
- **Step loop:** step() runs the 21 handlers in the contract's order. It calls the other strategy modules only when they exist, so it also runs alone. It stops on the tick of any stop event, a new dogfight or game end.
- **Skip idle time:** when nothing is in the air and no UFO is flying, the clock jumps to the next 10-minute boundary or the next landed-UFO take-off. A test proves the hash equals stepping 5 s at a time over a game week. I also checked this with the other engineers' real modules loaded: hashes match over 12 days.
- **Craft orders:** order, launch, recall and patrol give the contract's refusal reasons and warnings. Launch tops up the soldiers' equipment from base stores.
- **Flight:** interceptors aim at the predicted intercept point. A contact starts a dogfight (OV.Dogfight.create plus dogfightStart) when the craft is armed, fast enough and under the dogfight limit. Otherwise the craft shadows the UFO.
- **Arrivals:** a craft reaching a landed or crashed UFO, a terror site or an alien base waits there and gets a craftArrived prompt: 'mission' for a crewed transport, else 'none'. A point gives a patrol prompt; its home base lands it through the repair → rearm → refuel → ready chain.
- **Lost targets:** a target that is gone or no longer detected turns into a patrol point and a targetLost popup.
- **Fuel:** burned every 10 min at current speed. Low fuel triggers an automatic return, and a craft at 0 fuel still flies home.
- **Other handlers:** patrol discovery of alien bases, autosave days, and loseCraft.
- **Base attacks:** a retaliation Battleship reaching a base pushes baseAttack and calls Campaign.baseDefence.
- **Detection (every 30 min):** hyper-wave first, then keep tracking inside any radar, then automatic detection by an airborne craft's radar, then the per-base roll (sum of radar chance × (100 + visibility) / 100). A test over 2 000 rolls lands within ±3 % of the formula. Lost tracking, lastSeen and G.seen updates are in.

**Missions**
- **planMonth:** follows the §3.18 script. Month 0: Alien Research (Sectoids, base region, +120 min) plus first terror at +3 days. Month 1: terror, the seeded alien base within 4 000 nm, and one table mission with ×3 weights near the base.
- **Waves:** halved timers, one UFO spawned per wave entry, trajectories flown with each leg's altitude and speed %, landings (5 s over water; city points are never land-checked), take-off, exit.
- **Terror:** the objective Terror Ship becomes the terror site at the city, lasting 8–16 h. Expiry costs 1 000 points, logs terrorIgnored and gives followers targetLost.
- **Shoot-downs:** onUfoDown crashes on land with a 24–72 h site, destroys over water, scores, delays the next wave, and rolls retaliation from month 2.
- **Retaliation:** retaliation UFOs search for the X-COM base, then a Battleship flies the assault run.
- **Alien bases:** built when their mission completes. Supply runs are 6 %/day; a supply ship landing reveals the base if tracked. Agents reveal one base 50 %/month.
- **Infiltration:** a pending pact signs at month end (+150), and the mission restarts.
- **Races:** alien bases and Battleships avoid Mutons until a commander is interrogated.
- **Research trigger:** finishing the Martian Solution starts a retaliation at once.

**Runs and checks**
- 60 days with no player: about 0.2 s. Each run produces about 10 detections, landings, 2–3 terror sites and 1–2 alien bases by mid-February.
- With the real Economy loaded, a passive player gets the council game-over on 1 March, as the rules intend.
- Determinism: two runs give the same hash, and a JSON round-trip mid-run then continuing gives the same hash.
- A scratch end-to-end with the real Dogfight module works: detect → intercept → crash → Skyranger arrives with the 'mission' prompt.
- In the first 20 days the first detection comes at day 0.1–3.5 across 12 seeds, followed by several landed scouts the Skyranger can reach.
- No browser run; nothing in my scope renders.
deviations: ufoLost is pushed with stop:true only when a craft is following the UFO (orig: popup only with followers). The catalogue default ✔ is overridden through data.stop, so UFOs leaving radar don't pause the game for nothing.
ufoLanded, ufoLiftOff and ufoGone are pushed only for detected UFOs, so toasts never reveal hidden UFOs. landedUfoGone is pushed when an undetected landed UFO that a craft was targeting lifts off.

Alien-base missions build their base when the mission completes: all waves spawned and every UFO gone, even if X-COM shot some down. This keeps the month-1 'seedAlienBase' guarantee. For seedAlienBase, up to 8 zone-4 land points are drawn and the first within 4 000 nm of a base is kept (the closest otherwise).

A craft waiting over a ground target has status 'patrol', patrol:false and patrol speed (half fuel burn); only patrol:true crafts do alien-base discovery. After targetLost the craft keeps patrol:true and moves at patrol speed toward the last-seen point, with no second arrival popup. Ordering a patrol at the craft's own position starts patrolling at once, with no popup.
In contacts() (step 3), a UFO reaching a craft counts only if the craft can keep up (ufo.speed <= craft speed). An unarmed craft therefore doesn't 'teleport-shadow' a faster UFO.

RNG streams: the retaliation base-search roll (scan10m) and the infiltration pact country use 'ai'. Wave countdowns, crash/terror timers, waypoint points, supply and agent-reveal rolls use 'geo' (the contract is silent on scan10m).

Retaliation: once the base is spotted, the next spawn is the assault Battleship, an extra spawn even if the wave list was exhausted (countdown re-rolled from the last wave timer), then nothing more. It starts from a ring 25–35° around the target base.

Trajectory semantics: leg i→i+1 flies at pts[i] altitude and speed %. A point with altitude 0 means landing at the previous point (REA). Supply ships fly straight to their alien base and land there; the assault run flies straight to the X-COM base.

Extra exports beyond §5.3/§5.4: World.dropTarget, World.checkup, World.detectChance; Missions.removeUfo, Missions.regionWeights. G.alien gained pendingPacts, newPacts and lastReveal; they are documented in the missions.js header but not yet in the contract's §1.12 table.
The event interceptOrderInvalid is never emitted: no reliable one-shot trigger exists without per-craft state; the order-time warnings cover these cases.
No data change to js/data/geo.js was needed; new world/mission knobs went into TUNE instead.
open_issues: Suite: `node tools/test.js --strict` shows 511 passed, 1 failed. The failure is data_crossref.test.js › 'textos em pt-PT sem formas brasileiras comuns': up.archive «Arquivo X-COM» and up.menu.hint in pt-PT.ufopaedia.js (the Ufopaedia engineer's in-progress file). My files pass.

Pacing, terror race, needs a lead decision. The month-0 first terror (day 3–8) uses alien_terror month 0 = Sectoid 60 / Floater 40, and month 1 = Snakeman 60. The battle engineer measured both Sectoid (Cyberdiscs) and Snakeman (Chryssalids) terror at 0 % wins with month-1 gear on Veterano. I did not change raceSchedule because tools/tests/data_geo.test.js (not mine) pins these values. Suggested fix: alien_terror 0: {floater:70, sectoid:30} (the original's month-0 split), 1: {floater:60, sectoid:20, snakeman:20}, keeping Snakemen at 60 from month 2.

Pacing, infiltration: with wave timers ×0.5, a month-1 table infiltration completes in about 3 weeks. In seed 1 India signs a pact at the 1 March month end. That matches the data, but it is a fast funding bleed the player can only slow by shooting UFOs down. Worth watching in the campaign bot.

Gameplay note: many Europe zone-0 boxes are over sea, so interceptions there often end with 'crash over water ⇒ destroyed' (orig rule). That gives double score but no recovery mission. 2 of 3 crash outcomes in my 6-seed e2e run went this way.

Contract tidy-up for the architect: add G.alien.pendingPacts/newPacts/lastReveal to §1.12, and the extra exports World.dropTarget/checkup/detectChance and Missions.removeUfo/regionWeights to §5.3/§5.4. Economy currently finds new pacts through same-tick pactSigned events, which works; G.alien.newPacts and lastReveal are also available for the month report.

Two separate checkup functions now exist: World.checkup (used when a craft lands at its base) and BaseSim.checkup (used by Campaign.finishMission for Cydonia). They should stay identical (repair → rearm → refuel → ready).

basesim.summary:
I implemented the four strategy sim modules against CAMPAIGN_API.md and added 61 tests (all fast, under 0.15 s per file). The `--strict` suite is 492 passed, 1 failed, and the failure is not in my files: it is the pt-PT wording check on `up.archive` / `up.menu.hint`, which belong to the Ufopaedia engineer's in-progress i18n. All `geo_` and `core` tests (164) pass.

**Soldiers** (`OV.Soldiers`)
- `generate` makes the same draws as `Campaign.makeSoldier`, so `newCampaign` now uses it with no change in output.
- `applyMission` runs `OV.Morale.postMission`, promotes a rookie with secondary experience to squaddie, and adds missions and kills. Wound days are 25–75 % of HP lost, rounded up, and a wounded soldier leaves the craft.
- Promotions use the original top-down algorithm with our quotas (N/4, N/8, N/15, commander at N ≥ 20) and the original promotion score.
- Also done: daily healing, memorial on death, rename.

**Economy** (`OV.Economy`)
- Points are recorded by region and country using the original map rectangles.
- UFO activity: +1 per flying UFO and +2 per landed UFO every 30 min; alien bases add +5 per day.
- Starting upkeep is exactly $2 579 000. Pending personnel and craft deliveries are included in upkeep, as in the original.
- Funding change copies the original `Country::newMonth`, including the $1 000 steps, the cap, pacts and which random draws happen.
- The council bonus starts with the February report. Ratings get their labels and the council its text key.
- The month-end report matches the contract shape. History and reports keep 12 entries.
- Defeat triggers on two bad months, two month-ends in debt (with a warning the first time), or no base left.

**Bases** (`OV.BaseSim`)
- Facilities: placement rules, building (instant with the debug flag), and dismantling, which is refused if it would disconnect the base, remove the lift, or drop a capacity below what is in use.
- Capacities: quarters, labs, workshops, stores (counted in tenths of a unit), containment, hangars, radars, defences and hyper-wave. Pending deliveries count against capacity.
- Personnel and market: hire/sack with 48 h delivery; buy with 24 h items, 48 h craft weapons, the craft's own delivery time, and storage/hangar checks; sell immediately (live aliens never).
- Craft loadout: moving cargo, changing armour, assigning soldiers and fitting weapons all keep a craft's equipment covering its soldiers' loadouts.
- Research: cost is randomised 80–120 % on start; corpses and live aliens are consumed on start; daily progress; one completion path that sets researched, flags, Ufopaedia articles (including free ones), points, `Missions.onResearch` and the unlocked lists. Progress labels come from a key function.
- Production: paid per unit, engineer-hours per hour, continuous mode, stalls on funds/materials/hangar with one popup per stall, and resumes when resources return.
- Craft upkeep in the base: repair (+5 HP/h) → rearm (original clip arithmetic) → refuel (every 30 min, using Elerium for Elerium-fuelled craft) → `craftReady`. When craft ammo is delivered, ready craft go back to rearming.

**Dogfight** (`OV.Dogfight`)
- A tick-for-tick copy of OpenXcom's `DogfightState::update` (checked against the local source): approach 2, retreat 4, missiles move 8 per tick and are not dragged by the craft's own movement, out-of-range missiles are lost, beams and UFO shots resolve instantly.
- Craft weapons fire automatically when in range; reload depends on the mode; each weapon can be switched off.
- The UFO fires at one interceptor at a time and breaks off on the original countdown. Cautious mode pulls back to standoff once the craft has taken ≥ 50 % damage. A craft with no ammo left pulls back and the fight ends.
- Results go through `Missions.onUfoDown` or `World.loseCraft` as the contract says.

**Data fix:** interrogation topics now use the article `race_<race>` (contract §5.11). The Ufopaedia already maps both forms, so nothing breaks.
deviations: `Dogfight.create` returns null (and changes nothing) when the craft or UFO is missing, the craft is already fighting, the UFO is not flying, or `MAX_DOGFIGHTS` is reached. The contract only says it returns a dogfight.
When the UFO breaks off, Dogfight sets `ufo.speed` to the UFO's maximum speed, as OpenXcom does. The contract lists only Missions and World (plus Dogfight for damage) as writers of UFO fields.
Dogfight tick events gain two informative types for the overlay: `{t:'df.retreat'}` (Cautious pulled back after ≥ 50 % damage) and `{t:'df.breakOff'}` (the UFO is outrunning the craft).

'craftRetreated' is used when the craft has no ammo left and nothing in flight and has pulled back to standoff. The dogfight then ends, so it cannot hang. Cautious mode at ≥ 50 % damage switches the mode to standoff, as in the original, and does not end the fight.
Cautious and Standard target distances count only weapons that are switched on and still have ammo. OpenXcom ignores the on/off switch.
Placement accepts a facility touching one still under construction, as DESIGN §3.14 says. OpenXcom by default needs a finished one.
`startProduction` pays for the first unit straight away when it can; otherwise it sets `stalled` and pushes `productionStalled` immediately. The contract only describes paying each hour.
A craft repaired during an hour starts rearming in the same hour, which shortens turnaround slightly. Each hour rearms all weapons, not one.
When an Elerium-fuelled craft cannot refuel for lack of Elerium, it pushes `craftRearmShort` (what:'fuel') and becomes ready with partial fuel.

Extra helpers not in the contract: `BaseSim.staff`, `canHire`, `canBuy`, `checkup`, `loose`, `renameBase`, `renameCraft`, `researchLabel`; `Economy.baseUpkeep`, `councilBonus`, `councilKey`, `fundingChange`; `Soldiers.rename`, `quotas`, `woundDaysFor`, `RANK`.

BaseSim uses `Campaign.availableResearch` / `availableManufacture` when section B exists, and otherwise computes the same lists from Data. Dogfight falls back to a minimal crash/removal or craft-loss path only if `Missions.onUfoDown` or `World.loseCraft` is missing; this is used for debugging and is covered by a test.
open_issues: The one `--strict` failure is not in my files: the pt-PT wording check flags `up.archive` / `up.menu.hint` in the Ufopaedia engineer's i18n (`js/i18n/pt-PT.ufopaedia.js`).

Gameplay needs a decision. With the original dogfight numbers (approach 2 per tick, first missile only at tick 200) and an Interceptor in Standard mode over 60 seeds: Recruta vs Small Scout gives 29 destroyed / 16 crashed / 15 escaped. Veterano vs Small Scout gives 14 / 11 / 35. Veterano vs Medium and Large Scouts gives 33/60 and 39/60 crashed. Turning off the Stingray to fly cannon-only never brings a Small Scout down at Veterano (0/60), so there is no way to avoid destroying it. That works against DESIGN §14's tutorial-like first crash.

Measured alternative: `Data.dogfight.approach` 4 instead of 2. Veterano then gives Small Scout 38 destroyed / 20 crashed / 2 escaped; cannon-only gives 36 crashed / 24 escaped; Medium and Large Scouts crash 57/60 and 58/60. Fights become about 4.8 s of real time instead of 8.5 s. It is a single value in `js/data/crafts.js`, which I own, but changing it is a tuning call rather than a data fix, so I left the original value. Please confirm if you want it applied.
World engineer: on arrival at base please set the craft status with `OV.BaseSim.checkup(G, craftId)`, so the repair → rearm → refuel chain has one definition.

Base UI engineer, i18n keys needed. `base.err.<reason>` for: unavailable, research, lift, cells, overlap, notConnected, funds, empty, inUse, count, quarters, busy, noSoldier, away, hangar, storage, unsellable, stock, noCraft, base, wounded, seats, slot, scientists, labs, engineers, workshops, name. `ev.productionStalled.<funds|materials|hangar>`. `ev.craftRearmShort` with what ammo or fuel. Council text keys `council.pleased`, `council.satisfied`, `council.dissatisfied`.

Dogfight UI engineer: projectile `pos` is the distance flown from the craft, and a projectile arrives when `pos ≥ dist`. Beam weapons and UFO shots resolve in the same tick and leave no projectile. `df.retreat` and `df.breakOff` can drive status text.
The original funding rule means a country whose funding reaches $0 never recovers. It is faithful, but worth knowing when tuning.
